title: On-device inference adapter
content: Hexagon explores private mobile inference through Qualcomm NPU adapters; production NPU integration remains future work.
reason: Preserve a local-first path without overstating readiness.

title: No cloud dependency for core inference
content: The target architecture keeps sensitive prompt execution on the device when hardware support is available.

title: NPU bridge spike
content: A bridge contract was sketched for tokenizer, model session and streaming token events.

title: Embeddings adapter is future work
content: On-device embeddings are not part of the current Command Center demo and must not be presented as shipped.

title: Thermal budget matters
content: Sustained mobile generation must expose latency and thermal constraints to orchestration.

title: Provider boundary
content: Hexagon fits behind an inference provider interface and does not own memory, sessions or product UI.

title: Evidence source, not merged app
content: Command Center may cite Hexagon capabilities but will not merge Hexagon into its repository during Build Week.

title: Device matrix risk
content: Chipset, driver and quantization differences require capability detection and graceful fallback.

title: Durable evidence store
content: Project Memory persists episodes and versioned facts in SQLite with stable evidence identifiers.

title: Hybrid recall
content: Retrieval combines lexical candidates, structural expansion, dense similarity and declared rules.

title: Stable IDs improve inspection
content: Evidence IDs make answers auditable and let graph interactions open the original record.

title: Inactive facts stay out of recall
content: Facts marked inactive are retained for audit but excluded from ordinary retrieval.
reason: Preserve history without surfacing invalid knowledge.

title: Memory is model-independent
content: The durable memory layer exposes typed operations and does not require a particular language model.

title: Embedding cache benchmark
content: Content hashes avoided recomputing unchanged vectors during repeated recall runs.

title: Schema version remains one
content: Episode and fact rows retain schema version 1 while app storage uses an independent migration table.

title: Dense provider outage
content: A dense retrieval failure must return lexical and structural results with a degraded flag.

title: Chronological evidence
content: Episodes retain happened-at timestamps for timelines and decision reconstruction.

title: Visual memory control plane
content: Command Center is the visual control surface over Project Memory, Aria sessions, evidence graphs and guarded writes.

title: Typed input before voice
content: The required workflow ships with typed input; realtime voice is deferred until every submission gate passes.

title: Evidence drawer interaction
content: Graph and recall selections should open the same contextual evidence drawer.

title: No simulated persistence
content: All sessions, proposals and audit events shown by the interface must come from the API.

title: Five completed surfaces
content: The product surfaces are Aria, Recall Explorer, Knowledge Graph, Sessions and Timeline, and Audit.

title: Responsive panel study
content: Desktop uses a session rail, central canvas and evidence drawer; mobile uses full-screen panels and a dock.

title: Human-gated writes
content: Aria may persist a pending proposal but can never confirm its own memory write.

title: Ephemeral cloud workspaces
content: Cloud demo workspaces reset on instance restart and must clearly communicate their temporary lifetime.

title: Inspectable retrieval trace
content: Recall results expose signal scores, provenance, latency, embedding provider and degraded state.

title: One container demo
content: The static Next.js export and FastAPI service are packaged into one Cloud Run container.

title: Personal context source
content: LifeOS holds structured personal context that can inform an assistant when explicitly retrieved.

title: Consent boundary
content: Personal notes remain outside the public demo corpus and require explicit authorized connector access.

title: Small relevant context beats bulk export
content: Bounded retrieval produced clearer assistance than sending an entire personal archive.

title: Connector, not database merge
content: LifeOS should contribute evidence through an authorized adapter rather than sharing Command Center storage.

title: Sensitive body logging
content: Prompts and personal memory bodies must not be written to production application logs.

title: Evidence source only
content: LifeOS appears in the hero synthesis as an evidence source, not as a merged application.

title: Context freshness labels
content: Retrieved personal context benefits from visible timestamps and source labels.

title: No public user memory
content: The public corpus contains synthetic project facts only and no live LifeOS user records.

title: Low-friction intervention patterns
content: ADHD-SOS contributes concise, actionable interaction patterns for moments of executive friction.

title: Not medical advice
content: Supportive workflow suggestions must not be represented as diagnosis or medical treatment.

title: One next action
content: A single visible next action reduced interaction cost compared with a long generated plan.

title: Policy and UX evidence
content: ADHD-SOS informs interaction policy and accessible UX; it does not own the assistant runtime.

title: Mobile interruption recovery
content: Short session summaries helped users resume after leaving the app mid-task.

title: Evidence source only
content: ADHD-SOS remains a cited evidence source and is not merged into Command Center.

title: Notification overload
content: Assistant prompts should be user-initiated by default and avoid attention-grabbing notification loops.

title: Calm status language
content: Status updates should use direct calm language and make waiting states legible.

title: Private assistant architecture review
content: The review connected Hexagon inference, Project Memory evidence, Command Center UI, and bounded LifeOS and ADHD-SOS sources.

title: Fast private mobile assistant
content: A fast private mobile assistant pairs local inference adapters with durable local memory, visible evidence and narrowly scoped context connectors.

title: Cross-project paraphrase recall
content: Dense candidates recovered related mobile privacy records even when the query did not repeat their exact labels.
